messages:
Alex: Heads up — reproducible TS inference bug in the edge sample. Works in Node but fails during worker bundle types check.
Maria: Can you paste the minimal signature that's failing?
Alex: Sure: `export function request<T>(opts: { body: T }): Promise<string>; export function request(opts: { body: unknown }): Promise<string>;`
Alex: When calling `client.request({ body: {a:1} })` TS resolves body as unknown and complains `Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'T'`.
Sam: That smells like overload selection priority + inference break in the bundler resolution. What bundler/tsconfig are you using for the edge sample?
Alex: esbuild + tsc check. tsconfig: `module: "ESNext", moduleResolution: "Bundler", strict: true`. Local Node build (CJS) infers fine. Edge CI uses TS 5.1 in GH actions.
Lee: Two paths: adjust overload ordering so the generic signature is first, or change the fallback overload to use `any` instead of `unknown` for public API.
Maria: I'd rather keep `unknown` for safety. Could we add a thin helper `requestAs<T>(...)` generic wrapper that forwards to the implementation but keeps inference?
Sam: That's a good DX compromise. Also recommend shipping a sample tsconfig for Cloudflare/Edge that sets `moduleResolution: bundler` and explains TypeScript 5 differences so users copying samples don't get bitten.
Alex: I tried the wrapper and it works. Putting the generic signature first also fixed it. Switching fallback to `any` also fixed it but feels wrong.
Maria: CI action: ci-bot: run types-check on `samples/edge-*` against ts@5.1 and node 18.
ci-bot: queued types-check for samples/edge-quickstart (ts=5.1, node=18)
Lee: Could be our published `.d.ts` layout: ensure we publish declarations aligned with ESM output and exports map. Mismatched declaration entry points cause inference oddities sometimes.
Alex: I'll push a minimal repro to samples repo and open a PR with two fixes: (1) doc + sample tsconfig, (2) small overload reorder + helper wrapper. Tests included.
Sam: Please include a tiny changelog note for SDK breaking/behavioral change if we change public overloads.
Maria: Also file a follow-up to audit other public APIs using `unknown` — decide per-API whether to keep unknown or provide explicit overloads.
Lee: Agreed. Thanks Alex. After PR lands, publish canary typings and ask a couple of customers on Dedicated to smoke test if needed.
Alex: Will do, will link repro and PR here when ready.
Sam: Thanks :thumbsup:
